extracted.intended_audience: sellers and marketers offering negative-option features; legal counsel/compliance officers for online and offline merchants; consumer protection advocates; state and federal regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and final-rule requirements for merchants offering negative-option (auto-renew/subscription) features, covering what must be disclosed, how consent must be obtained and documented, placement/timing/format rules, recordkeeping, and enforcement principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of “material”
rubrics_metrics.description: Material means likely to affect a person's choice of, or conduct regarding, goods or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with section 5, the TSR, and longstanding Commission policy and case law. Mere puffery (e.g., “movies you will love,” “great cleaning every time”) is not material. Whether a misrepresentation of a privacy policy is covered depends on whether it is likely to affect consumer choice or conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on misrepresenting material terms or facts in connection with negative option sales
rubrics_metrics.description: The final Rule prohibits the specific practice of sellers misrepresenting material terms or facts in connection with negative option sales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission found record evidence of distinct harms from such misrepresentations (consumers often are charged repeatedly before detecting misrepresentation). This is treated as a specific deceptive practice under section 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required important information prior to obtaining billing information (§425.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must disclose all material terms prior to obtaining the consumer's billing information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission declined to limit required important information only to terms directly related to the negative option feature; disclosure before billing info is consistent with ROSCA and section 5. The Commission modified, clarified, and in some cases omitted elements of the originally proposed list to address comment concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure that consumers will be charged (including recurring charges) and trial-to-paid changes
rubrics_metrics.description: That consumers will be Charged for the good or service, or that those Charges will increase after any applicable trial period ends, and, if applicable, that the Charges will be on a recurring basis, unless the consumer timely takes steps to prevent or stop such Charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retained as a fundamental disclosure to combat deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of each deadline (by date or frequency) to act to prevent or stop Charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must disclose each deadline (by date or frequency) by which the consumer must act to prevent or stop the Charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies there may be multiple deadlines; 'frequency' includes irregular or conditional frequencies (e.g., within a certain period after notification that a new item is available) as well as regular schedules (e.g., the 15th of each month).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of the amount (or range) of costs (reasonable approximation allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must disclose the amount (or range of costs) the consumer will be charged, and, if applicable, the frequency of such charges a consumer will incur unless the consumer takes timely steps to prevent or stop those charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an exact figure is impossible (e.g., taxes or delivery depend on billing info), a reasonable approximation is acceptable (e.g., 'amount plus tax'). However, 'plus shipping' is not sufficient where shipping is beyond reasonable expectation; then an estimate of shipping costs is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of mandatory requirement to disclose dates each charge will be submitted (with exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final Rule omits the proposed mandatory disclosure of the date (or dates) each charge will be submitted for payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission agreed dates may be impossible or cumbersome to calculate and could reduce clarity of higher-priority disclosures. If disclosure of specific dates is necessary to prevent deception in an individual case, such disclosure is still required under §425.4(a), but placement is governed by §425.4(b)(2)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of information necessary to find the simple cancellation mechanism (§425.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must disclose 'The information necessary for the consumer to find the simple cancellation mechanism required pursuant to §425.6'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces a more detailed mandatory-step disclosure to provide concise upfront information while giving sellers flexibility so cancellation details do not crowd out other important disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement — certain mandatory disclosures must appear immediately adjacent to the means of recording consent (§425.4(b)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The four specific mandatory disclosures listed in §425.4(a) must appear immediately adjacent to the means of recording the consumer's consent for the negative option feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission removed ambiguous 'directly related to the negative option feature' language and confined adjacency to a narrow list to reduce burden and improve predictability. For voice transactions, 'immediately adjacent' means immediately before requesting and recording consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — other required disclosures must appear before seller obtains consumer consent (§425.4(b)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: All required disclosures not subject to the 'immediately adjacent' requirement must appear before the seller obtains consumer consent to the transaction pursuant to §425.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates a clear trigger event (the obtaining of consent) to determine when disclosures must be presented, addressing commenter concerns about vagueness of 'before consumers make a decision to buy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and conspicuous disclosures; must be 'unavoidable' (§425.4(b)(1) and §425.2(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each disclosure required by paragraph (a) must be clear and conspicuous. In interactive electronic media, a disclosure must be unavoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission deleted a prior absolute prohibition on requiring consumer action (e.g., clicking a hyperlink) to see a disclosure. Instead, disclosures must be unavoidable — e.g., sellers may prevent consent until a consumer has seen and acknowledged the disclosure (useful for space-constrained mobile displays). A disclosure that a consumer must take action to see is not per se excluded so long as it is unavoidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including 'other information' that interferes with the effectiveness of disclosures (§425.4(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers may not employ other information that interferes with, detracts from, contradicts, or otherwise undermines the ability of consumers to read, hear, see, or otherwise understand the required disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission omitted language that would have broadly prohibited 'any information not directly related' to material terms to avoid contradiction with other disclosure requirements. Nonetheless, adding extra adjacent disclosures that undermine the clarity of required disclosures will violate both the placement and the interference prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express, unambiguously affirmative consent to the negative option feature (§425.5(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must obtain a consumer's unambiguously affirmative consent to the negative option feature separately from any other portion of the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses consumers missing negative option features because they focus on other aspects (price, quality). The final Rule removed the proposed requirement to obtain separate consent to 'the rest of the transaction' (§425.5(a)(3)); that separate consent requirement was eliminated based on comments. For written offers, a checkbox, signature, or substantially similar method may be used to record affirmative consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping/verification of consent (three-year retention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must obtain and maintain verification of the consumer's consent; the Commission modified the proposed recordkeeping requirement to require sellers to maintain records for three years from the date of consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission sought comment on appropriate retention; commenters raised cost/privacy concerns. Final adoption limits retention to three years. (The proposed different longer periods were rejected.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplar consent mechanisms for written offers (§425.5(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For written offers (including internet), sellers may obtain unambiguously affirmative consent through a check box, signature, or other substantially similar method, which the consumer must affirmatively select or sign to accept the negative option feature; this consent must be independent from any other portion of the offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted such mechanisms may evolve; Commission provided exemplar, not exhaustive list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference to TSR for pre-acquired account information and free-to-pay conversions (§425.5(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers subject to the Rule must comply with all applicable provisions of the TSR (16 CFR part 310), including those related to pre-acquired account information and free-to-pay conversions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistency with existing TSR obligations (e.g., rules about using stored payment credentials and converting free trials to paid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures when consumer has previously saved billing information
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a consumer previously provided account information to the seller and expressly allowed the seller to store that information, the seller must make the required disclosures prior to obtaining the consumer's consent to use saved account information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies timing concerns raised by commenters regarding saved billing info and consent flows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of free trials and separate consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission invited comments on whether sellers offering free trials should be required to obtain an additional round of consent before charging at the end of a free trial; commenters were divided and the Commission modified some related provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some consumers and advocacy groups supported separate post-trial consent; many sellers argued separate consent is unnecessary given other Rule requirements and state laws. Final text removed separate consent for 'rest of the transaction' but left open how to treat certain free-trial scenarios within other requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement policy factor — when Commission will act based on consumer ability to police
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering whether to act against a deceptive practice, the Commission will observe the extent to which consumers themselves have been able to police and generate consequences for seller deception; when consumers can easily evaluate the product, are frequent purchasers, inexpensive items, the Commission will examine a practice closely before issuing a complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where market incentives constrain deception (e.g., repeat purchases encourage honesty), the Commission is less likely to proceed absent strong evidence. Conversely, where negative option features bypass ordinary re-evaluation and permit recurring charges, additional protection is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality exclusions — puffery examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Mere puffery is not material (examples: 'movies that you will love' or 'great cleaning every time').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These classic puffery examples are not within the scope of materiality and therefore do not trigger required disclosures or deception findings on their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: State AG recommendations (cancellation policies and retention)
rubrics_metrics.description: State AGs recommended sellers be required to disclose all material policies concerning cancellation, disclose all information necessary for the consumer to effectively cancel, prohibit 'click-here-to-cancel' icons that lead to oblique flows, and provide important information in a manner capable of being retained by the consumer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission considered these recommendations; final Rule revised cancellation disclosure language to require information necessary to find the simple cancellation mechanism (§425.6) rather than extensive upfront cancellation details. State AG recommendations inform enforcement emphasis on effective cancellation mechanisms and retention-capable disclosures.
